questions.text_english:
Read the following passage carefully:

(1) Cinnamon is a spice obtained from the inner bark of several tree species from the genus Cinnamomum. Cinnamon is made by cutting the stems of cinnamon trees. The inner bark is then extracted and the woody parts removed. When it dries, it forms strips that curl into rolls, called cinnamon sticks. These sticks can be ground to form cinnamon powder. The spice, consisting of the dried inner bark, is brown in colour and has a delicately fragrant aroma and a warm sweet flavour. The distinct aroma and flavour of cinnamon derive from its essential oil and principal component, cinnamaldehyde, as well as numerous other constituents including eugenol.

(2) There are two main types of cinnamon: Cassia and Ceylon. The two have different nutritional profiles. Ceylon cinnamon comes from Sri Lanka. Some people call it "true cinnamon." Cassia cinnamon, on the other hand, originates from southern China. Cassia is cheaper than Ceylon cinnamon. Cassia cinnamon has a robust, rich, somewhat bitter flavour while Ceylon is sweeter and lighter in flavor.

(3) Cinnamon was once more valuable than gold. In Egypt it was sought for embalming and religious practices. In medieval Europe it was used for religious rites and as a flavouring agent. Later it was the most profitable spice in the Dutch East India Company trade.

(4) Cinnamon is widely used as an aromatic condiment and flavouring additive in a wide variety of cuisines, sweet and savoury dishes, breakfast cereals, snack foods, bagels, teas, hot chocolate and traditional foods.

(5) Cinnamon is a spice that has been prized for its medicinal properties for thousands of years. In recent years, modern science has started to confirm many of the potential health benefits associated with cinnamon. Cinnamon has antimicrobial and antifungal properties, which is why it's often found in dental-hygiene products and is sold as cinnamon supplements. It is also a good source of antioxidants, substances that inhibit the effect of free radicals (reactive atoms that can damage cells). Due to its anti-inflammatory nature, cinnamon is currently being researched for its potential to fight Alzheimer's disease and decrease symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome and colon cancer.

(6) Studies also suggest that cinnamon has anti-diabetic properties, and may offer protection from cancer and cardiovascular disease, among other conditions. However, more evidence is needed to confirm cinnamon's benefits. In the short term, consuming moderate amounts of cinnamon as a spice or as a supplement seems to be safe for most people. However, cinnamon contains coumarin. This is a natural flavouring, but it also plays a role in creating warfarin, the common blood-thinning drug. Consuming too much coumarin can lead to liver damage and affect coagulation.
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer the following questions, based on the above passage.
questions.solution: Passage-based question set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the sentence appropriately. The characteristic aroma and flavour of cinnamon originate from its essential oil, primarily composed of ___________. Paragraph (1)
sub_questions.solution: According to paragraph (1), the distinct aroma and flavour of cinnamon derive from its essential oil and its principal component, cinnamaldehyde, along with other constituents including eugenol. Therefore, the characteristic aroma and flavour of cinnamon originate from its essential oil, primarily composed of cinnamaldehyde.

sub_questions.text_english: Based on the reading of the passage, examine, in about 40 words, how cinnamon derived from the trees is made fit to be used as a spice. Paragraph (1)

key_points: Stems of cinnamon trees are cut and inner bark is extracted
Woody parts are removed from the bark
The bark dries and curls into rolls called cinnamon sticks, which can be ground into powder

sub_questions.solution: To prepare cinnamon as a spice, the stems of cinnamon trees are first cut and the inner bark is carefully extracted, with the woody parts removed. As the bark dries, it naturally curls into rolls known as cinnamon sticks. These sticks are then ground to produce cinnamon powder, ready for use.

sub_questions.text_english: Mention one point of difference between Ceylon cinnamon and Cassia cinnamon. Paragraph (2)

key_points: Ceylon cinnamon has a sweeter and lighter flavour, while Cassia cinnamon has a robust, rich, and somewhat bitter flavour.

sub_questions.solution: One key difference between the two types is their flavour: Cassia cinnamon has a robust, rich, and somewhat bitter taste, whereas Ceylon cinnamon is sweeter and lighter in flavour. Additionally, Cassia is cheaper than Ceylon cinnamon.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the sentence appropriately. The author says that cinnamon was once more valuable than gold because ___________. Paragraph (3)

fill_values: it was highly sought after for embalming and religious practices in Egypt, for religious rites and as a flavouring agent in medieval Europe, and was the most profitable spice in the Dutch East India Company trade

sub_questions.solution: According to paragraph (3), cinnamon was once more valuable than gold because it was highly prized and sought after across civilisations — in Egypt for embalming and religious practices, in medieval Europe for religious rites and as a flavouring agent, and later as the most profitable spice in Dutch East India Company trade.

sub_questions.text_english: What is the tone of the writer in the given lines from paragraph (5)? Rationalize your response in about 40 words. "Cinnamon is a spice that has been prized for its medicinal properties for thousands of years."

key_points: The tone is informative and appreciative
The writer presents cinnamon's long medicinal history with admiration
The phrase 'prized for thousands of years' shows deep respect for its enduring value

sub_questions.solution: The tone of the writer in these lines is informative and appreciative. By stating that cinnamon has been 'prized' for medicinal properties for thousands of years, the writer conveys admiration for the spice's enduring significance. This establishes a sense of reverence and historical importance before introducing modern scientific validation.

sub_questions.text_english:
The writer's use of the phrases 'modern science has started to confirm' in paragraph (5) and 'more evidence is needed to confirm' in paragraph (6) suggests that the benefits of cinnamon are:
1. proven
2. scientific
3. uncertain
4. controversial
5. harmful

Select the correct option:
sub_questions.solution: Option (C) — only 3 (uncertain) — is correct. The phrase 'modern science has started to confirm' implies the process is ongoing and not yet conclusive, and 'more evidence is needed to confirm' directly suggests that the benefits are not fully proven. This points to uncertainty, not established fact, controversy, or harm.

sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following statements about cinnamon and its health benefits is true?

options_english.A: Modern science has evidence to prove that cinnamon has many anti-diabetic properties, and it offers complete protection from cancer and cardiovascular disease.
options_english.B: Cinnamon lacks antimicrobial and antifungal properties, making it unsuitable for dental hygiene products.
options_english.C: Antioxidants found in cinnamon have no effect on free radicals in the body.
options_english.D: Cinnamon's anti-inflammatory properties are being researched for its potential benefits in Alzheimer's disease, irritable bowel syndrome and colon cancer.

sub_questions.solution: Option (D) is correct. Paragraph (5) clearly states that due to its anti-inflammatory nature, cinnamon is currently being researched for its potential to fight Alzheimer's disease and decrease symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome and colon cancer. Options A, B, and C directly contradict information in the passage.

sub_questions.text_english: Which of the following statements best describes the author's attitude toward cinnamon and its uses?

options_english.A: Finds cinnamon to be a prized condiment which can be used in almost all food items.
options_english.B: Believes that cinnamon should be used by everyone, everyday.
options_english.C: Recognizes that cinnamon has many useful properties, including health benefits.
options_english.D: Believes that cinnamon should only be used as a medicinal supplement.

sub_questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. The author takes a balanced and informative approach throughout the passage, discussing cinnamon's culinary uses, historical significance, and medicinal properties while also noting the need for more scientific evidence. This reflects a measured recognition of cinnamon's wide range of useful properties, including health benefits, rather than any extreme view.

questions.text_english:
Read the following passage carefully:

(1) When planning vacations, Indians typically prioritize domestic destinations, as shown by Ministry of Tourism data indicating 1.7 billion domestic tourist visits within India compared to 21 million international departures in 2022. Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka stand out as the top states for domestic tourism. Reasons for domestic tourism are many, some travel because it suits their budget while others love to explore the historical, cultural diversity. The government today is focussing on tourist-friendly infrastructure which is making travel more convenient for the domestic traveller.

(2) In terms of outbound tourism, a significant proportion of Indian travellers, totalling 5.9 million, visited the United Arab Emirates in 2022, comprising 28 percent of total outbound tourist travel. Other Gulf states such as Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Kuwait also rank among the top destinations, with 2.4 million, 880,000, and 830,000 Indian visitors, respectively. Additionally, countries like the United States and the United Kingdom attract a considerable number of Indian tourists because these countries offer a mix of traditional and contemporary experiences along with enjoying unique cuisines and diverse landscapes.

(3) The popularity of Gulf States and the U.S. may be influenced by migration trends. The current issue of the International Organization for Migration's (IOM) World Migration Report highlights significant migration flows from India to the United Arab Emirates, the United States, and Saudi Arabia. For instance, the Emirates hosted approximately 3.6 million Indian migrants as of August 2023. Only via two corridors have more people transferred from one country to another as of 2020 according to the IOM: Mexico to the United States with around 11 million and Syria to Turkey with approximately 4 million. These migration corridors rank among the top ten globally.
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer the following questions, based on the above passage.
questions.solution: Passage-based question set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: What does the use of the phrase 'prioritise domestic destinations' by the writer, in paragraph (1) imply?

options_english.A: Indian tourists prefer places in the country itself.
options_english.B: Indian tourists like to stay at home.
options_english.C: Indian tourists mainly travel on low budgets.
options_english.D: Indian tourists love to hitch-hike and trek.

sub_questions.solution: Option (A) is correct. The phrase 'prioritise domestic destinations' means that Indian tourists give first preference to places within India rather than abroad. The data in paragraph (1) supports this — 1.7 billion domestic visits compared to only 21 million international departures in 2022 — clearly indicating a preference for in-country travel.

sub_questions.text_english: Fill in the blanks with the appropriate option from those given in brackets, based on your understanding of paragraph (2). The statement that, World Migration Report highlights significant migration flows from India to the United Arab Emirates, the United States, and Saudi Arabia, is a/an ________ (fact/opinion) because it is a/an __________ (subjective judgement/objective detail).
sub_questions.solution: The statement is a fact because it is based on the findings of the IOM World Migration Report, which provides verifiable, data-backed information about migration flows. It is an objective detail, not a personal opinion or subjective judgement, as it draws on documented statistical evidence from a recognised international organisation.

sub_questions.text_english: Draw a comparative analysis of domestic tourists travelling within India with domestic tourists travelling outside India in 2022. Answer in about 40 words.

key_points: 1.7 billion domestic tourist visits within India vs 21 million international departures in 2022
Domestic tourism far outnumbers outbound tourism
Budget suitability and cultural exploration drive domestic travel; migration links and diverse experiences attract outbound travellers

sub_questions.solution: In 2022, there were 1.7 billion domestic tourist visits within India, compared to only 21 million international departures. Domestic tourism is overwhelmingly higher, driven by budget considerations and cultural exploration. In contrast, outbound tourism, though smaller in scale, is attracted by diverse international experiences and is often linked to migration patterns.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the following with a suitable reason. Gulf states rank as popular destinations for Indians _________.

fill_values: because of significant Indian migration to these countries, creating strong personal and cultural ties that attract Indian tourists

sub_questions.solution: Gulf states rank as popular destinations for Indians because of the strong migration links between India and these countries. A large number of Indian migrants reside in nations like the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Kuwait, which naturally attracts Indian tourists who visit family and friends or are drawn by familiar communities and cultural ties.

sub_questions.text_english:
Select the option that is true for the Assertion and Reason given below:
Assertion: Indians prioritize Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh for domestic tourism.
Reason: These states are full of historical monuments.

options_english.A: Both the Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason is the correct explanation of the Assertion.
options_english.B: Both the Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of the Assertion.
options_english.C: The Assertion is true, but the Reason is false.
options_english.D: The Assertion is false, but the Reason is true.

sub_questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. The assertion is true — the passage mentions Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh as top states for domestic tourism. The reason is also generally true as both states do have historical sites. However, the passage cites multiple reasons for domestic tourism such as budget and cultural diversity, not specifically historical monuments, so the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the sentence appropriately. The fourthmost visited outbound destination for Indians to the Gulf is _________.
sub_questions.solution: According to paragraph (2), the top Gulf destinations for Indian outbound tourists are UAE (5.9 million), Saudi Arabia (2.4 million), Qatar (880,000), and Kuwait (830,000). Therefore, the fourthmost visited outbound Gulf destination for Indians is Kuwait.

sub_questions.text_english: Mention any two reasons for domestic tourism becoming popular.

key_points: Domestic travel suits the budget of many Indian tourists.
Travellers enjoy exploring India's historical and cultural diversity.

sub_questions.solution: According to the passage, two reasons for domestic tourism's growing popularity are: first, it suits the budgets of many Indian travellers who find it more affordable; and second, the rich historical and cultural diversity of India motivates people to explore different states. Additionally, improved tourist-friendly infrastructure has also made domestic travel more convenient.

sub_questions.text_english: What is the writer's view about the tourism industry in the west? Write any two points.

key_points: Western countries like the US and UK attract Indian tourists by offering a mix of traditional and contemporary experiences.
They also draw visitors through unique cuisines and diverse landscapes.

sub_questions.solution: According to paragraph (2), the writer views the western tourism industry, particularly the United States and United Kingdom, as highly attractive for Indian tourists. These countries draw visitors by offering a blend of traditional and contemporary experiences. They also appeal through their unique cuisines and diverse, picturesque landscapes, making them desirable international destinations.

sub_questions.text_english: Identify the word in paragraph (3) that indicates the 'preference' of people travelling to the Gulf.

key_points: popularity

sub_questions.solution: The word in paragraph (3) that indicates the preference of people travelling to the Gulf is 'popularity'. The paragraph begins with 'The popularity of Gulf States and the U.S. may be influenced by migration trends,' showing that these destinations are preferred and favoured by Indian travellers.

questions.text_english: Complete any ten of the following twelve tasks, as directed.
questions.instruction_line_english: Complete any ten of the following twelve tasks, as directed. (10×1=10)
questions.solution: Grammar tasks. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: Fill in the blank by using the correct form of the word in the brackets, for the given portion of a letter. I believe that with your support and ________ (cooperate), we can find a mutually agreeable solution that meets the expectations of all stakeholders involved.
sub_questions.solution: The blank requires a noun form of the verb 'cooperate' because it follows the conjunction 'and' paired with another noun 'support'. The correct noun form is 'cooperation'. The complete sentence reads: 'I believe that with your support and cooperation, we can find a mutually agreeable solution that meets the expectations of all stakeholders involved.'

sub_questions.text_english: Read the given sentence from an electric cooker's instruction manual. Identify the error and supply the correction in the sentence. For avoid damaging the appliance, do not immerse the electric cooker in water or any other liquid.
sub_questions.solution: The error is the use of 'avoid' after the preposition 'For'. When a preposition precedes a verb, the verb must be in its gerund (–ing) form. Therefore, 'avoid' should be corrected to 'avoiding'. The correct sentence reads: 'For avoiding damaging the appliance, do not immerse the electric cooker in water or any other liquid.'

sub_questions.text_english: Amit and Pallavi had a conversation about the inauguration of Pallavi's event. Report Amit's question. 'Did you manage to get any sponsors for the inauguration event scheduled for the next month?'

key_points: Amit asked Pallavi if/whether she had managed to get any sponsors for the inauguration event scheduled for the following month.

sub_questions.solution: In reported speech, the question is converted into an indirect statement. The auxiliary 'Did' becomes 'had', 'you' changes to 'she', 'next month' becomes 'the following month', and the question mark is dropped. The reported form is: Amit asked Pallavi if she had managed to get any sponsors for the inauguration event scheduled for the following month.

sub_questions.text_english:
Read the dialogue between Bharti and her mother, Geeta, regarding Geeta's birthday plans.
 Bharti: Do you want to go to a hill station on your birthday? 
Geeta: No, I want to stay at home and call my friends over.
 Select the correct option that reports the above dialogue. Bharti asked Geeta if she wanted to go to a hill station on her birthday. Geeta replied in the negative and said that __________.

options_english.A: she wanted to stay home and call her friends for celebrating.
options_english.B: I wanted to stay home and call my friends to celebrate.
options_english.C: she wanted to stay at home and call her friends over.
options_english.D: she wants to stay home by calling her friends to celebrate.

sub_questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. In reported speech, the first person pronoun 'I' changes to 'she' (referring to Geeta), and the present tense 'want' shifts to 'wanted' to maintain backshift. The phrase 'call my friends over' is accurately reported as 'call her friends over'. Option (A) changes the meaning, (B) incorrectly retains first person, and (D) uses wrong tense and preposition.

sub_questions.text_english: Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option, to complete the line of a notice placed on the notice board of a company. Please be informed that there will be a staff meeting in the conference room on Friday, 7th June, at 10:00 a.m. It is __________ for all to attend. (mandatory/obligatory/indispensable)
sub_questions.solution: The correct word is 'mandatory'. In the context of a formal office notice directing all staff to attend a meeting, 'mandatory' is the most appropriate word as it is commonly used in official and institutional contexts to mean 'required by authority or rule'. The sentence reads: 'It is mandatory for all to attend.'

sub_questions.text_english: Identify the error and supply correction for the given sentence from a preface of a book. Writing this book have been a journey of exploration and discovery.
sub_questions.solution: The error is the use of 'have' instead of 'has'. The subject of the sentence is the gerund phrase 'Writing this book', which is singular, and therefore requires the singular verb 'has'. The rule is: a gerund or gerund phrase used as a subject takes a singular verb. The corrected sentence reads: 'Writing this book has been a journey of exploration and discovery.'

sub_questions.text_english:
Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction for the opening line, from an analytical paragraph. 'The advent of social media has revolutionized communication by connected people across the globe in unprecedented ways.'
(A) has → have
(B) communication → communicating
(C) connected → connecting
(D) in → for
sub_questions.solution: Option (C) is correct. The error is 'connected', which is a past participle, used after the preposition 'by'. After a preposition, a verb must appear in its gerund (–ing) form. Therefore, 'connected' should be corrected to 'connecting'. The correct sentence reads: 'The advent of social media has revolutionized communication by connecting people across the globe in unprecedented ways.'

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the given entry in a personal diary, by filling the blank with the correct option. Today was a rollercoaster of emotions. It started off with a sense of excitement and anticipation as I __________ on a new project at work.
sub_questions.solution: Option (C) 'embarked' is correct. The sentence is a diary entry narrating past events, as indicated by the past tense verb 'started'. Since the diary entry describes what happened in the past, the simple past tense 'embarked' is appropriate. 'Embarking' (A) is a participle without an auxiliary, 'embark' (B) is present tense, and 'have embarked' (D) is present perfect, none of which match the past tense context.

sub_questions.text_english: Report the dialogue between a salesman and his customer, by completing the sentence. Salesman: I have a wide range of sportswear. Customer: Please show me something in cotton fabric, which is suitable for summers. The salesman stated ____________. The customer requested the salesman to show something in cotton fabric which would be suitable for summers.

fill_values: that he had a wide range of sportswear

sub_questions.solution: In reported speech, the salesman's statement 'I have a wide range of sportswear' is converted by changing 'I' to 'he', and the present tense 'have' shifts to 'had' due to backshift. The reported sentence reads: 'The salesman stated that he had a wide range of sportswear.'

sub_questions.text_english: Fill in the blank by choosing the correct option to complete an announcement on a flight. In thirty minutes, our flight attendants ________ meal service.
sub_questions.solution: Option (B) 'will begin' is correct. The sentence refers to a definite future action — meal service starting in thirty minutes — making the simple future tense 'will begin' most appropriate. Option (A) is grammatically incorrect as 'began' is a past form and cannot follow 'will'. Options (C) and (D) imply possibility or obligation, which do not suit a scheduled flight announcement.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the line from a 'Save the Environment' song, by filling the blank with the correct option. Pollution, pollution, its time to take a stand, / for the health of our planet, we've got to lend a hand, / Reduce, reuse, recycle, that's the key, / ________ our world for you and me.
sub_questions.solution: Option (B) 'to preserve' is correct. The blank requires an infinitive (to + base verb) to express purpose — the reason for reducing, reusing, and recycling. 'To preserve' correctly conveys the intent of protecting the world. Option (A) uses 'for' with a base verb, which is incorrect. Options (C) and (D) use a past participle 'preserved' after a preposition, which is grammatically wrong in this context.

sub_questions.text_english: Identify the error and supply the correction for the following instruction put up for safe use of elevators. Please refrain by standing near the door as it could lead to an accident.
sub_questions.solution: The error is the use of the preposition 'by' after 'refrain'. The correct collocation is 'refrain from', not 'refrain by'. The verb 'refrain' is always followed by the preposition 'from'. The corrected sentence reads: 'Please refrain from standing near the door as it could lead to an accident.'

sub_questions.text_english: As Anaisha/Anish Gupta of 84, Coral Apartment, Hoger Street, Viman Nagar, you feel that there has been a growing problem of illegal parking in the residential area of your neighbourhood, particularly near school and commercial establishments. This not only causes inconvenience to residents but also hampers the smooth flow of traffic and poses risks to pedestrians, especially children. Write a letter to the SHO of your city area, in about 120 words, stating the problem and requesting him to take necessary action for controlling the problem. Give suitable suggestions.

key_points: Proper letter format: sender's address, date, receiver's designation, subject line
Clear statement of the problem — illegal parking near schools and commercial areas
Impact: inconvenience to residents, traffic congestion, risk to pedestrians especially children
Suggestions: installation of no-parking signs, regular police patrolling, towing of illegally parked vehicles
Polite closing with request for prompt action

sub_questions.solution:
84, Coral Apartment,
Hoger Street, Viman Nagar
Date: 6th June, 2026

The SHO,
Viman Nagar Police Station

Subject: Complaint Regarding Illegal Parking in Residential Area

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to draw your kind attention to the growing menace of illegal parking in our residential locality, particularly near the school and commercial establishments on Hoger Street. Vehicles are being parked haphazardly on both sides of the road, severely obstructing the smooth flow of traffic and causing great inconvenience to residents. This poses a serious risk to pedestrians, especially school children.

I request you to kindly take strict action by deploying traffic personnel during school hours, installing no-parking signboards, and initiating towing of illegally parked vehicles. Your prompt intervention will be greatly appreciated.

Yours faithfully,
Anaisha Gupta

sub_questions.text_english: You are Yukti/Sanjay, the Head of Environment Club of Highways School, Hawapur. You feel concerned about the growing problem of single-use plastics and their detrimental impact on our environment. Their improper disposal is polluting our oceans, rivers and landscapes. Write a letter to the editor of a national daily, in about 120 words, suggesting measures to stop the use of single-use plastics to make a difference and mitigate the environmental impact of plastic pollution. Give suitable suggestions.

key_points: Proper letter format: sender's address, date, 'The Editor', subject line
Statement of concern about single-use plastics polluting oceans, rivers, landscapes
Suggestions: government bans, eco-friendly alternatives, public awareness campaigns
Call for community responsibility and educational initiatives
Polite closing requesting publication of the letter

sub_questions.solution:
Highways School,
Hawapur
Date: 6th June, 2026

The Editor,
The National Times

Subject: Urgent Need to Curb Single-Use Plastic Pollution

Dear Editor,

Through the esteemed columns of your newspaper, I wish to highlight the alarming rise of single-use plastics and their devastating impact on our environment. As head of our school's Environment Club, I have witnessed how improper disposal of plastic bags, bottles, and wrappers is choking our rivers, oceans, and landscapes.

I urge the government to strictly enforce the ban on single-use plastics, promote affordable eco-friendly alternatives such as cloth and paper bags, and run mass awareness campaigns in schools and communities. Citizens must also take individual responsibility by refusing plastic. Together, we can prevent irreversible environmental damage.

Yours sincerely,
Yukti

questions.solution: Analytical paragraph writing question. Model answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: Natural food, typically refers to food that has not been processed or preserved in any significant way before it is consumed, while ultra-processed food refers to food items that have been altered from their natural state through various methods. Given below is a table that differentiates between natural and processed foods. Study the description given and write an analytical paragraph in about 120 words, drawing a comparison between the two.

key_points: Introduction distinguishing natural and processed foods
Natural food: high fibre, healthy nutrients and fats, low sodium
Processed food: high sugar, unhealthy nutrients and fats, high sodium
Health benefits of natural food vs addictive appeal of processed food
Conclusion recommending natural food for long-term wellbeing

sub_questions.solution: Natural food and processed food represent two very different approaches to nutrition and health. Natural food, in its unaltered form, is rich in fibre, healthy nutrients, and healthy fats, while being low in sodium. It plays a vital role in regulating blood sugar and blood pressure, contributing significantly to overall wellbeing. In contrast, ultra-processed food contains high levels of sugar, unhealthy nutrients, unhealthy fats, and sodium. While it is undeniably tasty, ready to eat, and often addictive, it poses serious risks to long-term health. The convenience of processed food may attract many consumers, but the nutritional superiority of natural food is undeniable. Making informed dietary choices by prioritising natural food is essential for maintaining a healthy and balanced lifestyle.

sub_questions.text_english:
Social Media has a lasting impact on our thought process and influences our thinking in both positive and negative ways. With the help of the given cues and using your own ideas, write an analytical paragraph on 'The Impact of Social Media on Teenagers' in about 120 words.
POSITIVE: connects peers, creative expression, access information, community building.
NEGATIVE: impacts self-esteem, cyber bullying, privacy intrusion, distraction and addiction.

key_points: Introduction stating social media's dual impact on teenagers
Positive: connects peers globally, enables creative expression, provides access to information, builds communities
Negative: damages self-esteem, leads to cyberbullying, invades privacy, causes distraction and addiction
Balanced conclusion urging responsible use

sub_questions.solution: Social media has emerged as one of the most powerful influences on teenagers today, shaping their thoughts, relationships, and identities in both positive and negative ways. On the positive side, it connects peers across the globe, fosters creative expression through art, writing, and videos, enables easy access to information, and facilitates meaningful community building. However, the negative consequences are equally significant. Constant exposure to idealised images and opinions adversely impacts teenagers' self-esteem. Cyberbullying has become a growing menace, causing serious psychological harm. Privacy intrusion and the misuse of personal data are serious concerns. Moreover, excessive screen time leads to distraction and addiction, hampering academic performance. Therefore, while social media offers valuable opportunities, teenagers must learn to use it responsibly and with critical awareness.

questions.text_english:
Read the following extracts and answer the questions for any one of the given two, (a) or (b).
 He felt certain that his wings would never support him; so he bent his head and ran away back to the little hole under the ledge where he slept at night. Even when each of his brothers and his little sister, whose wings were far shorter than his own, ran to the brink, flapped their wings, and flew away, he failed to muster up courage to take that plunge which appeared to him so desperate. His father and mother had come around calling to him shrilly, upbraiding him, threatening to let him starve on his ledge unless he flew away. But for the life of him he could not move.  (Two Stories about Flying – His First Flight)
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the following extracts and answer the questions for any one of the given two, (a) or (b).
questions.solution: Extract-based question. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: State any one inference about the parents of the baby seagull from the given statement. 'His father and mother had come around calling to him shrilly, upbraiding him, threatening to let him starve on his ledge unless he flew away.' (Two Stories about Flying – His First Flight)

key_points: The parents were concerned about their young one's development and used tough love to push him towards achieving his first flight.

sub_questions.solution: One inference about the parents of the baby seagull is that they were determined and tough in their approach to parenting. Rather than being sympathetic to his fear, they employed tough love — scolding, threatening, and withholding food — indicating their firm belief that their chick was capable of flying and needed only to overcome his fear.

sub_questions.text_english: Where did the little seagull sleep at night? (Two Stories about Flying – His First Flight)

key_points: The little seagull slept at night in a little hole under the ledge.

sub_questions.solution: According to the extract from 'His First Flight', the little seagull slept at night in a small hole under the ledge. When he was afraid to fly, he bent his head and ran back to this familiar shelter, which provided him a sense of security away from the terrifying prospect of leaping into the air.

sub_questions.text_english: Which factors contributed to the young seagull's reluctance to fly despite the encouragement and threats from his parents? Elaborate in about 40 words, with reference to the extract. (Two Stories about Flying – His First Flight)

key_points: The young seagull was convinced his wings could not support him in flight
The leap into the vast open air appeared desperate and terrifying to him
His fear was so overwhelming that even watching his siblings fly successfully could not motivate him

sub_questions.solution: The young seagull's reluctance to fly stemmed from deep-rooted fear and self-doubt. He was firmly convinced that his wings would never support him, and the act of leaping off the ledge seemed utterly desperate and dangerous to him. Even watching his siblings — with shorter wings — fly successfully could not overcome his paralysing fear.

sub_questions.text_english: Which phrase or word would correctly substitute 'muster up' in the given sentence from the extract? He failed to 'muster up' courage to take that plunge which appeared to him so desperate.
sub_questions.solution: Option (D) 'gather' is the correct substitute for 'muster up'. The phrase 'muster up courage' means to collect or summon one's courage, which is closest in meaning to 'gather courage'. Option (A) 'review' means to examine, (B) 'resolve' means to determine, and (C) 'distribute' means to spread out — none of these appropriately replace 'muster up' in this context.

sub_questions.text_english: Tricki was tottering along in his little tweed coat.... He struggled on, drooping in his harness. I thought it wouldn’t be long before I heard from Mrs. Pumphrey. The expected call came within a few days. Mrs. Pumphrey was distraught. Tricki would eat nothing. Refused even his favourite dishes; and besides, he had bouts of vomiting. He spent all his time lying on a rug, panting. Didn’t want to go for walks, didn’t want to do anything. I had made my plans in advance. The only way was to get Tricki out of the house for a period. I suggested that he be hospitalized for about a fortnight to be kept under observation. The poor lady almost swooned. She was sure he would pine and die if he did not see her every day. But I took a firm line. Tricki was very ill and this was the only way to save him.  (A Triumph of Surgery)'
Why had the author made his plans in advance? (A Triumph of Surgery)

options_english.A: Mrs. Pumphrey was worried that Tricki would pine and die without her.
options_english.B: The author was aware of the severity of Tricki's medical condition.
options_english.C: The author knew about Mrs. Pumphrey's financial condition.
options_english.D: The author had planned his own vacation.

sub_questions.solution: Option (B) is correct. The author, Mr. Herriot, had observed Tricki's deteriorating condition — the dog was tottering, drooping, and struggling even during walks — and had already assessed the severity of his illness. This foresight prompted him to plan in advance that Tricki would need to be removed from the house and hospitalised. Options A, C, and D are not supported by the extract.

sub_questions.text_english: The author firmly proposed the need to remove Tricki from the house for a specified period. Elaborate the reason for doing so in about 40 words. (A Triumph of Surgery)

key_points: Tricki was seriously ill — refusing food, vomiting, and lethargic
The author believed Mrs. Pumphrey's overindulgence was causing Tricki's illness
Hospitalisation for a fortnight under observation was the only way to restore Tricki's health

sub_questions.solution: The author proposed removing Tricki from Mrs. Pumphrey's home because Tricki was dangerously ill — refusing food, vomiting, and spending all his time lying down. The author understood that Mrs. Pumphrey's excessive pampering and overfeeding were the root causes. Hospitalisation under medical observation for a fortnight was the only way to save Tricki.

sub_questions.text_english: Fill in the blank with the correct word from the brackets. The word 'swooned' in the following sentence indicates almost ________ (tripped/fainted).
sub_questions.solution: The correct word is 'fainted'. The word 'swooned' means to lose consciousness momentarily due to an extreme emotional shock. In the extract, Mrs. Pumphrey almost swooned upon hearing the suggestion that Tricki be hospitalised, indicating she nearly fainted from distress. 'Tripped' means to stumble and does not carry the same emotional connotation.

sub_questions.text_english: 'Mrs. Pumphrey was distraught.' What does this suggest about her character? Mention any one reason. (A Triumph of Surgery)

key_points: Mrs. Pumphrey was deeply emotional and excessively attached to Tricki, treating him more like a child than a pet, which is why the prospect of being separated from him caused her such extreme distress.

sub_questions.solution: The statement 'Mrs. Pumphrey was distraught' reveals that she was deeply emotional and excessively attached to Tricki. She treated him as if he were her child rather than a pet, which is evident from her fear that he would 'pine and die' without her. This reflects her over-indulgent and emotionally dependent nature.

questions.text_english: Read the following extracts and answer the questions for any one of the given two, (a) or (b).
questions.instruction_line_english: Read the following extracts and answer the questions for any one of the given two, (a) or (b).
questions.solution: Poetry extract-based question. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english:
Some say the world will end in fire
Some say in ice.
From what I’ve tasted of desire
I hold with those who favour fire. 

             (Fire and Ice)
The speaker offers evidence to support his preference for one theory over the other. Mention the evidence. (Fire and Ice)

key_points: The speaker's personal experience of desire — 'From what I've tasted of desire' — serves as evidence to support his belief that fire (symbolising desire) could bring about the end of the world.

sub_questions.solution: The speaker uses his own personal experience of desire as evidence to support his preference for the fire theory. He states 'From what I've tasted of desire,' suggesting that he has personally experienced the consuming and destructive power of desire, which convinces him that fire — representing passionate, unchecked human emotions — is capable of destroying the world.

sub_questions.text_english: What is the prediction of the poet about how the world will come to an end? Answer in about 40 words. (Fire and Ice)

key_points: The poet presents two theories: the world will end either in fire or in ice
He personally favours fire, symbolising desire and passion
He concedes that ice, symbolising hatred and indifference, would also suffice for destruction

sub_questions.solution: In 'Fire and Ice', Robert Frost predicts that the world will end either in fire or in ice. He personally sides with fire, which symbolises burning desire and passion, believing it could destroy the world. However, he acknowledges that ice — representing cold hatred and indifference — would also be equally capable of causing the world's end.

sub_questions.text_english: 'Fire' and 'Ice' are used in the poem as _______.
sub_questions.solution: Option (B) 'metaphors' is correct. In the poem 'Fire and Ice', fire and ice are not literally compared using 'like' or 'as' (which would make them similes), but are directly used to represent human emotions — fire stands for desire and passion, while ice stands for hatred and cold indifference. This direct symbolic substitution makes them metaphors.

sub_questions.text_english: Comment on the overall mood of the extract. (Fire and Ice)

key_points: The overall mood of the extract is reflective and ominous, with the poet calmly contemplating the destructive capacity of human emotions and the inevitable end of the world.

sub_questions.solution: The overall mood of the extract from 'Fire and Ice' is reflective and darkly philosophical. The poet calmly contemplates the two possible ways the world could end, giving the poem an ominous undertone. Despite the gravity of the subject — the destruction of the world — the tone remains controlled and matter-of-fact, which makes it even more unsettling.

sub_questions.text_english:
The leaves strain toward the glass
small twigs stiff with exertion 
long-cramped boughs shuffling under the roof
like newly discharged patients
half-dazed, moving 
to the clinic doors.

     (The Trees)
How does the comparison between the boughs and newly discharged patients contribute to the theme or message of the poem? Answer in about 40 words. (The Trees)

key_points: The simile shows the trees are weakened after being confined indoors, just like patients are weak after hospitalisation
It reinforces the poem's theme of nature struggling to reclaim its freedom from human control
The comparison highlights the slow but determined movement of nature back to its natural habitat

sub_questions.solution: The comparison between boughs and newly discharged patients in 'The Trees' reinforces the poem's central theme of nature reclaiming its freedom. Just as patients are weakened and disoriented after confinement, the long-cramped boughs move slowly and uncertainly towards freedom. This simile powerfully illustrates nature's determined struggle against human domestication and control.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the sentence with the appropriate option. The imagery and descriptions in the poem create a mood of ______________________.
sub_questions.solution: Option (B) 'transition and uncertainty' is correct. The poem 'The Trees' describes leaves straining toward glass, twigs stiff with effort, and boughs shuffling like half-dazed patients — all images that suggest a slow, uncertain movement from confinement to freedom. This creates an overarching mood of transition — from captivity to nature — accompanied by hesitation and uncertainty about the outcome.

sub_questions.text_english: Fill in the blank with one word. The stiff movement of the twigs in the above extract suggests the ______________ . (The Trees)
sub_questions.solution: The stiff movement of the twigs in the extract from 'The Trees' suggests the struggle or effort of nature to break free from the confines of the human-built indoor space. The word 'stiff with exertion' implies that the twigs are putting in enormous effort, having been held captive for long, to move towards the open air and reclaim their natural space.

sub_questions.text_english: Why does the poet describe the bough as 'shuffling'? (The Trees)

key_points: The boughs are described as 'shuffling' because they have been cramped indoors for a long time and move slowly and awkwardly, like patients who have just been discharged from a clinic, still weak and disoriented.

sub_questions.solution: The poet describes the boughs as 'shuffling' because they have been cramped and confined indoors for a long time and are now slowly and awkwardly making their way towards freedom. The movement is slow and laboured, much like that of newly discharged patients, reflecting both physical weakness from long confinement and a tentative reclaiming of natural space.

questions.text_english: Answer any four of the following five questions in 40–50 words each. (4×3=12)
questions.instruction_line_english: Answer any four of the following five questions in 40–50 words each.

sub_questions.text_english: How was Mij to be transported to England? (Mijbil the Otter)

key_points: The author had to transport Mij in a box as per airline regulations
The box had to be a certain size with ventilation holes
Mij was to be carried in the aircraft's hold, not in the cabin

sub_questions.solution: In 'Mijbil the Otter', Mij was to be transported to England by aeroplane. According to the airline's regulations, Mij had to be kept in a small wooden box with adequate ventilation. The box was placed in the aircraft's hold rather than the cabin, which caused the author great anxiety about Mij's comfort and safety during the long journey.

sub_questions.text_english: Why did Anne think that paper has more patience than people? (From the Diary of Anne Frank)

key_points: Anne felt lonely and had no true confidante among people
She believed people would not listen to her deeper thoughts without judging or dismissing them
Paper, being inanimate, accepts everything written without reaction or judgment

sub_questions.solution: In 'From the Diary of Anne Frank', Anne believed paper had more patience than people because she felt deeply lonely and had no true friend to whom she could pour out her innermost thoughts without fear of judgement. People, she felt, would not listen seriously or would respond critically. A diary, being inanimate, accepts all thoughts silently and without reaction.

sub_questions.text_english: How did the baker herald his arrival every morning? (Glimpses of India – A Baker from Goa)

key_points: The baker announced his arrival by the jingling sound of his bamboo or the specially made bamboo staff
He banged it on the ground while walking, creating a characteristic sound
The sound would wake up the children who eagerly awaited his arrival

sub_questions.solution: In 'A Baker from Goa', the baker heralded his arrival every morning by the distinctive jingling sound made by his bamboo staff as he banged it on the ground. This familiar sound would rouse the children from sleep, who would eagerly rush out to greet him. The sound became an inseparable part of the fond childhood memories associated with the baker.

sub_questions.text_english: Describe how the poem 'The Trees' brings out the conflict between man and nature.

key_points: Trees are confined inside the human-built house, stripped of their natural freedom
They are straining towards the glass and moving slowly to reclaim their place in the forest
The poem shows nature's resistance against human domestication and control

sub_questions.solution: In 'The Trees' by Adrienne Rich, the conflict between man and nature is portrayed through the image of trees trapped inside a human dwelling. The leaves strain toward the glass, and the boughs shuffle toward the door, desperately seeking to return to the open forest. The poem suggests that humans have displaced nature, but nature silently and persistently resists, striving to reclaim its freedom.

sub_questions.text_english: How did Valli manage to gather information about the bus ride she was planning? (Madam Rides the Bus)

key_points: Valli listened carefully to conversations between neighbours and adults about the bus
She asked discreet questions to gather details about the fare, distance, and timings
She planned meticulously and saved money to fund her trip

sub_questions.solution: In 'Madam Rides the Bus', Valli gathered information about her planned bus ride through careful observation and discreet questioning. She listened attentively to conversations between neighbours and adults about the bus journey to the nearest town. She asked casual but pointed questions to find out the fare, the distance, and the timing of the bus, and saved money by resisting small temptations to fund her adventure.

sub_questions.text_english: How did Ausable get rid of Max? (The Midnight Visitor)

key_points: Ausable cleverly invented the story of a nonexistent balcony outside his window
When a knock came at the door, he told Max it was the police
Panicked, Max stepped out through the window expecting to reach the balcony, but fell to his death

sub_questions.solution: In 'The Midnight Visitor', Ausable cleverly tricked Max by inventing the existence of a balcony outside his hotel room window. When a knock came at the door, Ausable claimed it was the police. Terrified of being caught, Max stepped out of the window expecting to land on the imaginary balcony, and fell to the ground below, allowing Ausable to escape safely.

sub_questions.text_english: Why does Mme Loisel hastily depart from the ball when her husband places a modest wrap on her shoulders? (The Necklace)

key_points: Mme Loisel is embarrassed by the contrast between the modest wrap and her elegant ballgown
She fears the other rich women will notice her humble wrap and look down upon her
She wants to preserve the illusion of wealth and elegance that she has enjoyed at the ball

sub_questions.solution: In 'The Necklace', Mme Loisel hurriedly departs from the ball when her husband places a modest, everyday wrap on her shoulders because she is deeply embarrassed. She fears that the other richly dressed women will notice the stark contrast between her plain wrap and her elegant gown, thereby exposing her true social status and shattering the illusion of wealth she had maintained all evening.

sub_questions.text_english: 'In time you will be more learned than anyone else in the village. Then no one will ever be able to laugh at you.' What effect did her teacher's words have on Bholi? Elaborate. (Bholi)

key_points: The teacher's encouraging words gave Bholi hope and confidence for the first time
Bholi felt someone believed in her despite her stammering and pockmarked appearance
Her teacher's words motivated her to study hard and transformed her into a confident, educated person

sub_questions.solution: The teacher's kind and encouraging words had a deeply transformative effect on Bholi. For the first time in her life, someone believed in her potential despite her stammering and pockmarked face. These words filled Bholi with hope, confidence, and a desire to study hard. They ultimately helped transform her from a timid, neglected girl into a courageous and self-assured educated woman.

questions.text_english: Answer any one of the following two questions in 100–120 words.

questions.solution: Long answer literature questions. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text_english: Analyse and evaluate the role of faith in 'A Letter to God' and 'The Sermon at Benares'.

key_points: In 'A Letter to God', Lencho's unwavering faith in God drives the entire narrative
Despite the hailstorm destroying his crops, he writes to God with complete trust
In 'The Sermon at Benares', the Buddha's teachings emphasise acceptance over blind faith
Kisa Gotami's faith in the Buddha leads her to wisdom about the universality of death
Contrast: Lencho's faith is naive and literal; Buddha's teaching guides rational acceptance

sub_questions.solution: Faith plays a central and contrasting role in both 'A Letter to God' and 'The Sermon at Benares'. In 'A Letter to God', Lencho's faith in God is absolute and childlike. When a hailstorm destroys his entire crop, he does not despair but writes a letter directly to God, requesting a hundred pesos. His faith is so deep that he even suspects the post office employees of stealing when the full amount does not arrive, rather than doubting God. In 'The Sermon at Benares', Kisa Gotami's faith in the Buddha leads her on a journey of profound realisation. The Buddha does not offer her a miracle but uses her own experience to teach that death is universal and grief must be accepted. While Lencho's faith is literal and simplistic, the Buddha channels Gotami's faith into wisdom and inner peace. Both stories demonstrate that faith, when tested, can lead to transformation — either deeper belief or enlightened understanding.

sub_questions.text_english: Explore the contrasting images of the tiger in 'A Tiger in the Zoo' and the tiger in 'How to Tell Wild Animals'.

key_points: In 'A Tiger in the Zoo', the tiger is caged, helpless, and stripped of its natural dignity
The tiger paces restlessly in its cage, symbolising the loss of freedom
In 'How to Tell Wild Animals', the tiger is described humorously as fierce and dangerous in its natural habitat
The contrast highlights captivity vs freedom and tragedy vs comedy
Both poems together present a complete picture of the tiger — noble in the wild, broken in captivity

sub_questions.solution: The two poems present strikingly contrasting images of the tiger. In Leslie Norris's 'A Tiger in the Zoo', the tiger is a captive, pacing restlessly in a locked cage, its magnificent strength rendered powerless. The poet evokes a sense of pathos as the tiger stalks a few steps, its velvet paws and brilliant eyes reflecting suppressed rage and sorrow. This image is deeply sympathetic and critical of human interference with nature. In contrast, Carolyn Wells's 'How to Tell Wild Animals' presents the tiger in a comic and exaggerated light. The wild tiger in its natural habitat is described humorously — one who leaps upon you and hugs you tightly until you are dead. This playful tone highlights the tiger's ferocity through absurd humour. Together, the two poems offer a complete portrait of the tiger: noble, fierce, and free in the wild, but broken, sad, and restrained in captivity. The contrast makes a powerful statement about the impact of human civilisation on nature's most magnificent creatures.

sub_questions.text_english: 'Brilliant scientist though he was, Griffin was rather a lawless person.' Elaborate. (Footprints without Feet)

key_points: Griffin was a brilliant scientist who discovered the formula for invisibility
He used his gift to commit crimes — burning his landlord's house and robbing shops
He stole money from a clergyman's house and terrorised the village of Iping
His lawlessness escalated, showing a complete disregard for human life and society
His scientific genius was wasted because he lacked moral responsibility

sub_questions.solution: Griffin, the central character in H.G. Wells's 'Footprints without Feet', is indeed a paradox — a man of extraordinary scientific brilliance but deeply flawed moral character. He successfully discovered the rare scientific formula that rendered the human body invisible, a remarkable intellectual achievement. However, instead of using this discovery for the benefit of mankind, Griffin exploited it for entirely selfish and criminal ends. He set fire to his landlord's house out of revenge, stole from a London store, robbed a theatrical shop, and pilfered money from the clergyman's home. In the village of Iping, his invisible presence caused widespread panic and fear among the residents. His behaviour escalated from petty theft to open violence, showing a complete disregard for law and human dignity. His genius was overshadowed entirely by his lawlessness. Griffin's story is a cautionary tale about the dangerous consequences of great scientific power in the hands of an irresponsible and morally corrupt individual.

sub_questions.text_english: How and when did Hari Singh meet Anil? Why did Hari Singh lie that he knew how to cook? (The Thief's Story)

key_points: Hari Singh met Anil at a wrestling match where Anil was watching the wrestlers
Hari Singh approached Anil with his charming and friendly manner
He lied about knowing how to cook so that Anil would employ him as a cook and give him a place to stay
His real intention was to get close to Anil and rob him
Anil was an easy-going young man who agreed to let Hari stay and teach him to cook and write

sub_questions.solution: In Ruskin Bond's 'The Thief's Story', Hari Singh, a fifteen-year-old experienced thief, met Anil at a wrestling match. Anil was watching the wrestlers with an amused expression when Hari approached him with a friendly and confident manner. Recognising Anil as a simple, easy-going young man who could be easily befriended and later robbed, Hari introduced himself cleverly. When Anil asked if he knew how to cook, Hari promptly lied and said he could cook, though he actually had no such knowledge. He did this deliberately — his intention was to gain Anil's trust, secure a place to stay, and eventually steal from him when the opportunity arose. Anil, being a kind-hearted and generous person, agreed to take Hari in as a cook and even promised to teach him how to read and write. Hari's lie was a calculated move to establish the proximity he needed to execute his plan of theft.
